---
title: "Tips on tables"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Put the detail in a tip, not in another column. The row says "Reds", and the tip says how many games they won and who
coaches them. A reader gets the detail without a second page.

`tip_table()` puts a tip on the rows, cells and headers of a `DT::datatable()` or a `reactable::reactable()` table. The
tip is drawn from the row's own values, and it follows the row when the reader sorts, filters or changes the page.

## One tip for every row

Give `rows` a string with `{{ column }}` placeholders. Each row is its own record.

```{r}
library(hovercraft)

scores <- data.frame(
  team = c("Reds", "Blues", "Greens"),
  wins = c(12, 9, 4),
  losses = c(3, 6, 11),
  coach = c("A. Reviewer", "B. Reviewer", "C. Reviewer")
)

tip_table(
  DT::datatable(scores),
  rows = "**{{ team }}**: {{ wins }} wins, {{ losses }} losses. Coach: {{ coach }}"
)
```

Every placeholder is checked against the table's columns in R. A name that is not a column stops with an error that lists
the columns you can use, not with an empty tip in the browser.

`reactable` works the same way:

```{r}
tip_table(
  reactable::reactable(scores),
  rows = "**{{ team }}**: {{ wins }} wins, {{ losses }} losses"
)
```

## A tip for one column

`cells` takes one entry per column, by name. `headers` does the same for the header cells, which have no row to read
from, so a header tip is words or a template with no placeholders.

```{r}
tip_table(
  DT::datatable(scores),
  cells = list(wins = "{{ wins }} wins this season, {{ losses }} losses"),
  headers = c(wins = "Games the team won this season")
)
```

A cell's tip wins over its row's. A column you leave out has no cell tip; `NA` or `""` says so on purpose.

A target that needs its own settings (a side, a look, a long form) takes a `tip_spec()` in place of words. Only `rows` can
also pin and send events:

```{r}
tip_table(
  DT::datatable(scores),
  rows = tip_spec("{{ team }}: {{ wins }} wins", placement = "right", pin = TRUE, events = "pin"),
  cells = list(wins = "{{ wins }} wins this season"),
  id = "scores"
)
```

## Show where the tips are

A cell with a tip looks like any other until the reader rests the pointer on it. `marker = "corner"` draws a small triangle in the corner
of each cell and header cell that has one, as a spreadsheet does for a note. A row takes no marker, so `marker` needs `cells`
or `headers` too. The corner is the only marker a table draws for now.

## Keyboard

A table row cannot take focus by itself. `tip_table()` gives the table one tab stop. The arrow keys then move between the
rows, cells and headers that have a tip, Home and End go to the ends of a row, and Ctrl with Home or End to the ends of
the table. The tip shows for what has focus. A click on a row selects it, as it always did, so a row tip does not pin on
click: it pins with the pin button or the `P` key.

## Pins and the server

Give the table an `id` and a `tip_spec(pin = TRUE)` for `rows`, and a reader can pin the tip of a row. Add `events = "pin"` to the spec and the
server gets `input$scores_pin`. `max_pins` in `tip_table()` sets how many of the table's rows stay open at once, apart from
`use_hovercraft(max_pins = )`; all pins on a page together stop at 10, and at one on a screen narrower than 600 pixels.

To open, close or change one tip from the server, give `tip_show()`, `tip_hide()` or `tip_update()` the table's `id` and
the address of the tip: `row` alone is a row, `row` with `column` is a cell, and `column` alone is a header cell.

```{r}
observeEvent(input$jump, tip_show("scores", row = 2, column = "wins"))
```

## Limits worth knowing

- `row` is the row's place in the data the table has now. A row that is not on the current page has no element yet, so
  `tip_show()` and `tip_update()` do nothing for it until it is. A `DT` table in server mode has only the rows of the
  current page on screen.
- The table's script does some work for each row on screen, so page a long table. In R, `tip_table()` reads the data once to
  check the columns, so it takes longer the more rows you give it.
- `tip_table()` is experimental in 0.1.0. Its shape may change, and the help page lists what was tried in a browser
  (`DT` with `scrollX`, `scrollY`, `fixedHeader`, `colReorder`, `responsive` and server mode, `reactable` with selection,
  `groupBy` and `details`).

The book has a part on tables, with live figures for rows, cells, headers, pins and the server: see
[The book](the-book.html). For the tip itself, see [Get started](hovercraft.html).
